targets.researchQuestion: Can the acquisition cash bridge and customer-concentration treatment be closed from the latest primary filing without speculative end-customer naming?
targets.gate: acquisition cash bridge and defensible customer/concentration treatment
targets.summary: Resolved sufficiently for Chief review. The Aug. 1, 2026 10-Q gives a reproducible acquisition/cash bridge and both contracting-party and end-customer concentration tables. Future insourcing remains a non-gating uncertainty, not a reason to leave CRDO active indefinitely.
evidence: Cash fell from $1.165B at May 2, 2026 to $466.9M at Aug. 1, 2026; short-term investments were $297.4M at Aug. 1. Operating cash flow was +$90.2M, investing cash flow -$762.0M and financing cash flow -$26.7M for the quarter.

DustPhotonics purchase consideration was $1.251B: $769.6M cash, $169.1M ordinary shares, $2.5M replacement-equity consideration and $310.0M contingent consideration. The filing records $10.0M of contingent consideration as liability and $300.0M as equity.
Direct/contracting-party revenue concentration for the quarter: Customer A 43%, Customer B 28%; accounts receivable concentration: A 57%, B 28%.
Issuer-supplemented end-customer concentration: Customer D 33%, Customer C 28%, Customer E 13%, Customer F 10%. This resolves the reporting-vs-end-customer ambiguity without inferring identities.
inference: The filing supports a quantitatively bounded liquidity/acquisition view and demonstrates extreme but explicitly measurable concentration. The unidentified customer labels do not prevent concentration-risk scoring if methodology requires magnitude rather than identity.

unknowns.reason: Forward competitive outcome; current filing already quantifies concentration exposure.

falsifiers: A later primary filing materially revises DustPhotonics purchase accounting/cash consideration or concentration percentages.
Methodology explicitly requires named end-customer identity rather than concentration magnitude.

targets.researchQuestion: Can governance/control ownership and customer-concentration treatment be resolved from the 2026 proxy and latest 10-Q, while separating future warrant vesting from a true gate?
targets.summary: Resolved sufficiently for Chief review. The 2026 proxy gives current beneficial ownership and the latest 10-Q quantifies direct customer concentration. Amazon warrant vesting is real dilution context but future vesting uncertainty is not itself a gating blocker once the warrant terms are documented.
evidence: 2026 proxy as of March 1, 2026: FMR 13.7%, Vanguard 7.0%, BlackRock 6.1%; co-founders Jitendra Mohan 4.5% and Sanjay Gajendra 4.3%; all current executives/directors as a group 10.4%. The proxy reports no known related-person transactions since the beginning of fiscal 2025 under its review standard.

Latest June 30, 2026 10-Q revenue concentration: Customer A 29%, B 25%, C 15%, D 13% for Q2; six-month concentration A 29%, B 21%, C 17%, D 13%. Accounts receivable concentration at June 30: A 30%, B 17%, D 12%, E 10%.
The 10-Q explicitly notes certain listed customers are manufacturing partners purchasing on behalf of end customers, so direct-customer percentages may not equal underlying end-customer demand.

Amazon transaction agreement/warrant dated Feb. 5, 2026 permits up to 3,262,299 shares at $142.82 with vesting tied to up to $6.5B of qualifying Amazon-affiliate purchases; this is a documented dilution/customer-linkage mechanism rather than an unknown instrument.
inference: Governance/control can be scored from disclosed ownership without inventing control rights. Customer concentration is high and directly quantified. Amazon's commercial warrant increases economic alignment and dilution exposure, but exact future vesting is conditional and should stay outside the hard promotion gate unless methodology explicitly requires forecasting future vesting.

unknowns.reason: Conditional on future purchases; instrument size and trigger are already known.

unknowns.reason: Magnitude is disclosed; identities are not necessary unless methodology explicitly requires them.

A later filing materially changes the concentration table or Amazon warrant terms.

targets.researchQuestion: Is AI/customer concentration sufficiently quantified in the latest primary filing for methodology risk treatment?
targets.summary: Resolved sufficiently for Chief review using the Sept. 10, 2026 10-Q. Concentration is not merely qualitative: one semiconductor distributor was 50% of quarterly revenue and the top five end customers were about 55% of quarterly revenue. The filing explicitly ties concentration risk to AI customers, order timing, financing models and customer-owned tooling.
evidence: Q3 FY2026 10-Q: one semiconductor-solutions distributor accounted for 50% of fiscal-quarter net revenue and 46% of three-quarter net revenue.
Top five end customers, through all channels, were approximately 55% of Q3 net revenue and 50% of three-quarter net revenue.
Sales to distributors were 56% of three-quarter net revenue.

The risk section explicitly states AI customers may cancel/reduce/delay orders, use customer-owned tooling, or require leasing/deferred-payment structures, including Broadcom purchase-and-lease arrangements and the AI XPV platform, creating counterparty and asset-value exposure.
Q3 AI semiconductor revenue was $16.7B, up 221% year over year; this establishes the materiality of the AI concentration channel.
inference: The concentration gate can be scored conservatively without naming the end customers. Identity secrecy is secondary to the disclosed magnitude and contractual/financing risk pathways.

unknowns.item: Exact identity/share of each top-five end customer
unknowns.reason: Issuer provides aggregate concentration and direct-distributor concentration sufficient for risk magnitude; exact identities remain undisclosed.

falsifiers: A methodology rule explicitly requires named-customer mapping rather than concentration magnitude.
A later filing materially changes the concentration percentages.

targets.researchQuestion: Can backlog cancellation/conversion quality and customer-concentration treatment be closed from primary filings, or should the unresolved portion be made binary instead of staying vaguely active?
targets.gate: customer concentration plus cancellation/reschedule and backlog-conversion quality
targets.summary: Backlog-quality semantics are resolved; single-customer concentration remains unquantified in public filings reviewed. Chief should not leave VRT indefinitely active on a vague combined blocker. Split the gate: backlog/cancellation treatment is ready for review; customer concentration is either a documented issuer-nondisclosure handled conservatively or, if methodology truly requires numeric single-customer concentration, VRT should be blocked with that exact missing source path.
evidence: 2025 10-K: backlog was $15.0B at Dec. 31, 2025 versus $7.2B a year earlier; majority considered firm and expected within 12-18 months.

The same filing states customers can in some circumstances reduce or defer firm orders, usually with penalties or other termination consequences; acquired-business contracts may have differing reduction/termination terms.

2026 Q2 10-Q confirms strong current liquidity ($2.81B cash/equivalents plus $300M short-term investments and $2.484B revolver availability) but does not provide a named/single-customer concentration percentage in the reviewed disclosure.

The 10-K describes large cloud/hyperscale, neocloud and colocation providers as a material portion of the customer base with enhanced purchasing leverage and project/schedule-risk transfer, but does not quantify a top-customer percentage.
inference: Backlog should be treated as high-quality but not equivalent to non-cancellable revenue. Cancellation/reschedule risk is explicitly bounded by contract penalties/termination consequences, though not eliminated.

Absence of a disclosed >10% customer is not proof of diversification. If no methodology rule requires a numeric top-customer figure, preserve customer concentration as a conservative unknown/risk penalty rather than a promotion blocker.

unknowns.item: Numeric single-customer or top-five revenue concentration
unknowns.reason: Primary filings reviewed do not quantify it. It is gating only if the locked methodology explicitly requires a numeric concentration figure for promotion.

falsifiers: A current filing or investor disclosure provides numeric customer concentration.
Methodology confirms qualitative concentration treatment is sufficient; then this remaining item becomes non-gating.

systemBlindSpotInvestigation.researchQuestion: Are repeated-attempt blockers being expanded by optional unknowns rather than narrowed to locked methodology requirements?
systemBlindSpotInvestigation.summary: Yes, there is evidence of blocker bundling. ALAB future warrant vesting, AVGO exact customer identities, CRDO future insourcing and VRT future capacity normalization are forward/optional uncertainties that should not by themselves keep a company active once current required evidence is sufficient. Chief should preserve them as explicit unknowns/risk inputs while making binary ready/block decisions on the actual locked gate.
